context_requirements: Functional L-type or T-type voltage-gated calcium channels (CACNA1C/D or CACNA1G/H/I) expressed on the cell surface
Calcium-dependent signaling pathway active (e.g., calcineurin-NFAT) for transcriptional consequences
Cell context where calcium influx contributes to survival/proliferation signaling
falsifiers: No change in any of the listed proximal or late genes at 6 h or 24 h in any cell line
Strong upregulation of proliferation genes (e.g., CCNA2, CCNB1, MYC) at 24 h
No difference in response between cell lines known to express L-type channels (e.g., HT29, A549) and those that do not (e.g., HA1E)
Lack of any dose-dependent transcriptional effect across the nine cell lines

evidence.supports: Nifedipine inhibits calcium influx, impairs NFAT2 nuclear translocation, and suppresses colorectal cancer proliferation and metastasis, suggesting transcriptional effects on proliferation and immune-related genes.
Flunarizine, a T-type calcium channel blocker, protects against cisplatin-induced apoptosis in auditory cells, indicating a role in modulating cell death pathways.

Benidipine, a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker, prevents lysophosphatidylcholine-induced injury and ROS production in human aortic endothelial cells, linking calcium channel blockade to oxidative stress and apoptosis modulation.
Benidipine suppresses expression of angiogenic growth factors (VEGF, bFGF, TGF-beta1) and prevents cardiac remodeling in a diabetic rat model, suggesting effects on growth factor transcription.
Selective L-type calcium channel blocker S-312-d protects neurons from apoptosis by preventing Ca2+ influx, indicating a role in survival signaling.
